question.prompt: Triangle ABC is rotated about C to obtain triangle A′B′C, with A′ lying on side AB and \(\angle A=65^\circ\). Find the angle of rotation \(\angle ACA'\). (Unit: degrees)

solutions.explanation:
Assume first that \(A'\ne A\). After rotation, \(CA'=CA\). Since \(A'\) lies on side \(AB\), \(\angle CAA'=\angle CAB=65^\circ\). Thus \(\triangle CAA'\) is isosceles, so its other base angle is also \(65^\circ\). Therefore,
\[
\angle ACA'=180^\circ-2\times65^\circ=50^\circ.
\]
If \(A'=A\) is allowed, the zero rotation also satisfies the stated conditions and gives \(\angle ACA'=0^\circ\). Hence the keyed answer is \(50^\circ\) under the additional assumption \(A'\ne A\); without excluding coincidence, the answer is not unique.
solutions.title: Separate the distinct-point and coincidence cases
